title: Unital star algebra and positive normalized state

items.title: Unital star algebra and positive normalized state
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
A **unital complex star algebra** is a complex vector space $A$ with a complex-bilinear associative product $(a,b)\mapsto ab$, a specified unit $1_A$, and a conjugate-linear map $a\mapsto a^*$ such that, for all $a,b\in A$,

$$ (ab)^*=b^*a^*,\qquad (a^*)^*=a,\qquad 1_A^*=1_A. $$

A **positive normalized state** on $A$ is a complex-linear functional $\omega:A\to\mathbb C$ such that $\omega(1_A)=1$ and $\omega(a^*a)$ is a real nonnegative number for every $a\in A$. This is an algebraic definition: no norm, topology, boundedness condition, or completion is part of the data.
items.strategy: Definition with explicit algebraic operations and state conditions; no proof supplied.

references.title: Konrad Schmüdgen, An Invitation to Unbounded Representations of *-Algebras on Hilbert Space, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 285, Springer Nature (2020), §2.4, Definition 2.32
references.locator: §2.4, printed pp. 20–21: positivity and normalized states on a unital complex *-algebra.

references.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, lecture notes, arXiv:1904.04051v2 (2019), §§2.2–2.3

items.title: Positive-state Cauchy–Schwarz and left radical
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a unital complex star algebra and let $\omega$ be a positive normalized state on $A$ ([[def-qft-involutive-algebra-state]]). Define $q(a):=\omega(a^*a)$ and $N_\omega:=\{a\in A:q(a)=0\}$. Then

$$|\omega(b^*a)|^2\le q(a)q(b)\qquad(a,b\in A).$$

The form $(a,b)_\omega:=\omega(b^*a)$ is Hermitian and positive semidefinite, $N_\omega$ is its radical and a complex linear subspace, and $N_\omega$ is a left ideal: $c a\in N_\omega$ whenever $a\in N_\omega$ and $c\in A$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Put $X:=\omega(a^*b)$ and $Y:=\omega(b^*a)$. Positivity makes both $q(a+b)=q(a)+X+Y+q(b)$ and $q(a+ib)=q(a)+iX-iY+q(b)$ real; their imaginary parts give $\operatorname{Im}(X+Y)=0$ and $\operatorname{Re}(X-Y)=0$, hence $Y=\overline X$. Thus $(a,b)_\omega=\omega(b^*a)$ is Hermitian. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Suppose $q(b)>0$. For every $z\in\mathbb C$, positivity and the star-algebra laws give $0\le q(a+zb)=q(a)+zX+\overline z\,\overline X+|z|^2q(b)$. Taking $z=-\overline X/q(b)$ yields $0\le q(a)-|X|^2/q(b)$, so $|\omega(b^*a)|^2=|Y|^2=|X|^2\le q(a)q(b)$. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Suppose $q(b)=0$. If $X\ne0$, taking $z=-t\overline X$ for real $t>q(a)/(2|X|^2)$ makes $q(a+zb)=q(a)-2t|X|^2<0$, contradicting positivity. Hence $X=Y=0$, so the same Cauchy–Schwarz inequality holds when $q(b)=0$; if instead $q(a)=0$ and $q(b)>0$, step 2.1 forces $Y=0$ as well. [given, F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 If $a\in N_\omega$, steps 2.1 and 3.1 give $(a,b)_\omega=0$ for every $b\in A$; conversely $(a,a)_\omega=0$ means $a\in N_\omega$. Thus $N_\omega$ is exactly the radical and is a linear subspace. For $c\in A$, set $d:=c^*ca$. Applying Cauchy–Schwarz to $a,d$ gives $|\omega(d^*a)|^2\le q(a)q(d)=0$, while $d^*a=a^*c^*ca=(ca)^*(ca)$; therefore $ca\in N_\omega$. [F1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

references.title: Konrad Schmüdgen, An Invitation to Unbounded Representations of *-Algebras on Hilbert Space, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 285, Springer Nature (2020), §2.4 Proposition 2.33 and §4.4 Lemma 4.35
references.locator: §2.4, printed pp. 20–21, Hermiticity and Cauchy–Schwarz; §4.4, printed p. 78, null left ideal and quotient pairing.

references.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, lecture notes, arXiv:1904.04051v2 (2019), §2.3
references.locator: §2.3, state positivity, Cauchy–Schwarz and the null left ideal used in the GNS construction.

items.title: GNS Hilbert reconstruction with invariant operator domain
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a complex vector space with a complex-bilinear associative product, unit $1_A$, and conjugate-linear involution satisfying $(ab)^*=b^*a^*$, $(a^*)^*=a$ and $1_A^*=1_A$. Let $\omega:A\to\mathbb C$ be complex-linear with $\omega(1_A)=1$ and real nonnegative $\omega(a^*a)$ for every $a\in A$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Put $N_\omega:=\{a\in A:\omega(a^*a)=0\}$ and $\mathcal D_\omega:=A/N_\omega$, with

$$([a],[b])_\omega:=\omega(b^*a),$$

using the first-variable-linear convention. Let $H_\omega$ be the Hilbert completion of this inner-product space, and identify $\mathcal D_\omega$ with its canonical dense image in $H_\omega$. For each $a\in A$ define left multiplication on the common domain $\mathcal D_\omega$ by $\pi_\omega(a)[b]:=[ab]$. Then $\pi_\omega$ is a unital algebra representation of $A$ on the invariant dense domain $\mathcal D_\omega$, and

$$\mathcal D_\omega\subseteq D(\pi_\omega(a)^*),\qquad \pi_\omega(a)^*|_{\mathcal D_\omega}=\pi_\omega(a^*).$$

Each $\pi_\omega(a)$ is closable, meaning that the closure of its graph in $H_\omega\times H_\omega$ is the graph of an operator. The vector $\Omega_\omega:=[1_A]$ is a unit cyclic vector, $\pi_\omega(A)\Omega_\omega=\mathcal D_\omega$, and $\omega(a)=(\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega,\Omega_\omega)$. For uniqueness, let $K$ be a Hilbert space, $\mathcal D'\subseteq K$ a dense linear subspace invariant under every operator $\rho(a)$, and $\rho:A\to\operatorname{End}(\mathcal D')$ a unital algebra representation satisfying $(\rho(a)x,y)=(x,\rho(a^*)y)$ for all $a\in A$ and $x,y\in\mathcal D'$. If $\Omega'\in\mathcal D'$, $\mathcal D'=\rho(A)\Omega'$, and $\omega(a)=(\rho(a)\Omega',\Omega')$, then there is a unique unitary $V:H_\omega\to K$ with $V\Omega_\omega=\Omega'$ and $V\pi_\omega(a)x=\rho(a)Vx$ for all $a\in A$ and $x\in\mathcal D_\omega$. This theorem supplies neither a C*-norm nor essential self-adjointness of $\pi_\omega(a)$ when $a=a^*$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By [F1], $N_\omega$ is a subspace and every element of it pairs to zero with every element of $A$. Thus $([a],[b])_\omega=\omega(b^*a)$ is independent of both representatives; it is Hermitian and nonnegative, and $([a],[a])_\omega=0$ holds exactly when $a\in N_\omega$, so the quotient pairing is positive definite. [F1, given]

1.2 For $a,b\in A$, replacing $b$ by $b+n$ with $n\in N_\omega$ changes $ab$ by $an\in N_\omega$ because $N_\omega$ is a left ideal by [F1]; hence $\pi_\omega(a)[b]=[ab]$ is well defined. Bilinearity, associativity and $1_A$ give $\pi_\omega(a+b)=\pi_\omega(a)+\pi_\omega(b)$, $\pi_\omega(\lambda a)=\lambda\pi_\omega(a)$, $\pi_\omega(ab)=\pi_\omega(a)\pi_\omega(b)$ and $\pi_\omega(1_A)=I_{\mathcal D_\omega}$, and left multiplication keeps $\mathcal D_\omega$ invariant. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F2] to the quotient inner-product space $\mathcal D_\omega$; under the stated Countable Choice assumption this gives the Hilbert completion $H_\omega$ and a dense isometric embedding of $\mathcal D_\omega$, which we identify with its image. This is the only completion invoked. [F2, given, step 1.1]

2.2 For $a,b,c\in A$, the quotient form gives $(\pi_\omega(a)[b],[c])_\omega=\omega(c^*ab)=([b],\pi_\omega(a^*)[c])_\omega$. By the definition of the Hilbert-space adjoint, this identity for all $[b]\in\mathcal D_\omega$ shows $[c]\in D(\pi_\omega(a)^*)$ and $\pi_\omega(a)^*[c]=\pi_\omega(a^*)[c]$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.3 Since $([1_A],[1_A])_\omega=\omega(1_A)=1$, $\Omega_\omega$ is a unit vector. Also $\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega=[a]$ for every $a\in A$, so its algebraic orbit is exactly $\mathcal D_\omega$ and is dense. Finally $(\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega,\Omega_\omega)_\omega=([a],[1_A])_\omega=\omega(a)$, recovering the state. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2]

2.4 Let $(H',\mathcal D',\rho,\Omega')$ be another algebraically cyclic *-representation of $A$ with common invariant dense domain $\mathcal D'=\rho(A)\Omega'$, $\rho(a^*)=\rho(a)^*|_{\mathcal D'}$, and $\omega(a)=(\rho(a)\Omega',\Omega')$. Define $U[a]:=\rho(a)\Omega'$. If $[a]=[0]$, then $\|\rho(a)\Omega'\|^2=\omega(a^*a)=0$, so $U$ is well defined; and for $a,b\in A$, $(U[a],U[b])=\omega(b^*a)=([a],[b])_\omega$ by the representation's adjoint identity. Thus $U$ is an isometry from $\mathcal D_\omega$ onto the dense subspace $\mathcal D'$. [given, F1, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 Suppose $x_n\in\mathcal D_\omega$, $x_n\to0$ in $H_\omega$, and $\pi_\omega(a)x_n\to y$ in $H_\omega$. For each $z\in\mathcal D_\omega$, step 2.2 gives $(y,z)_\omega=\lim_n(\pi_\omega(a)x_n,z)_\omega=\lim_n(x_n,\pi_\omega(a^*)z)_\omega=0$. Density forces $y=0$. Therefore the closed graph relation of $\pi_\omega(a)$ contains no two distinct outputs over one input: their difference would be a nonzero pair $(0,y)$. The graph closure is a graph, so $\pi_\omega(a)$ is closable. In particular, if $a=a^*$ then $\pi_\omega(a)$ is symmetric on $\mathcal D_\omega$; this does not prove essential self-adjointness. [step 2.2, given]

4.1 The isometry extends uniquely from the dense domain to a unitary $\overline U:H_\omega\to H'$ because its range $\mathcal D'$ is dense. It sends $\Omega_\omega$ to $\Omega'$ and, for $[b]\in\mathcal D_\omega$, $\overline U\pi_\omega(a)[b]=\rho(ab)\Omega'=\rho(a)\overline U[b]$; hence it intertwines the representations on the common domains. Uniqueness follows because every vector of $\mathcal D_\omega$ has the form $\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega$. [step 2.3, step 2.4, step 1.2] ∎

references.title: Konrad Schmüdgen, An Invitation to Unbounded Representations of *-Algebras on Hilbert Space, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 285, Springer Nature (2020), §§2.4 and 4.4
references.locator: §2.4, printed pp. 20–21; §4.4, printed pp. 78–81, especially Lemma 4.35, Proposition 4.36 and Theorem 4.38.

references.locator: §2.3, printed pp. 7–9: GNS theorem, quotient construction, common-domain representation, state recovery and uniqueness.

items.title: State-preserving symmetries implemented unitarily
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the hypothesis of [[thm-qft-algebraic-gns-domain]]. Let $G$ be a topological group with identity $e$. Let $A$ be a unital complex star algebra with positive normalized state $\omega$, and let $\alpha:G\to\operatorname{Aut}^*(A)$ be a group action: each $\alpha_g$ is a bijective complex-linear map preserving product, unit and involution, with $\alpha_e=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha_g\alpha_h=\alpha_{gh}$. Suppose $\omega(\alpha_g(a))=\omega(a)$ for all $g\in G$ and $a\in A$. Also suppose that, for every $a,b\in A$, the coefficient function $g\mapsto\omega(b^*\alpha_g(a))$ is continuous at $e$.

Use the GNS representation from [[thm-qft-algebraic-gns-domain]], with common dense domain $\mathcal D_\omega$ and cyclic vector $\Omega_\omega$. Then $U_g[a]:=[\alpha_g(a)]$ extends to a strongly continuous unitary representation $U:G\to\mathcal U(H_\omega)$, fixes $\Omega_\omega$, and satisfies

$$U_g\pi_\omega(a)U_g^{-1}|_{\mathcal D_\omega}=\pi_\omega(\alpha_g(a))\qquad(a\in A,g\in G).$$

Here strongly continuous means that $g\mapsto U_g\xi$ is norm-continuous for every $\xi\in H_\omega$. No differentiability, generator domain or spectral theorem follows from these hypotheses alone.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 If $n\in N_\omega$, then $\omega((\alpha_g n)^*\alpha_g n)=\omega(\alpha_g(n^*n))=\omega(n^*n)=0$, so $\alpha_g(N_\omega)\subseteq N_\omega$. Applying the same argument to $g^{-1}$ gives equality. For $a,b\in A$, $([\alpha_g(a)],[\alpha_g(b)])_\omega=\omega(\alpha_g(b^*a))=\omega(b^*a)$, so $[a]\mapsto[\alpha_g(a)]$ is an isometry on $\mathcal D_\omega$ with inverse induced by $\alpha_{g^{-1}}$; it extends uniquely to a unitary $U_g$ on $H_\omega$. The action law gives $U_gU_h=U_{gh}$, and $U_g\Omega_\omega=\Omega_\omega$. [F1, A1, given]

2.1 For $[b]\in\mathcal D_\omega$, $U_g\pi_\omega(a)U_g^{-1}[b]=U_g[a\alpha_{g^{-1}}(b)]=[\alpha_g(a)b]=\pi_\omega(\alpha_g(a))[b]$, using the representation rule and multiplicativity of $\alpha_g$. This is the claimed covariance identity on the common domain. [F1, A1, step 1.1]

2.2 For $a\in A$, state invariance and the quotient inner product give $\|U_g[a]-[a]\|^2=2\omega(a^*a)-\omega(a^*\alpha_g(a))-\omega((\alpha_g(a))^*a)$. The first cross term tends to $\omega(a^*a)$ as $g\to e$ by [A2]. For the second, invariance gives $\omega((\alpha_g(a))^*a)=\omega(\alpha_{g^{-1}}((\alpha_g(a))^*a))=\omega(a^*\alpha_{g^{-1}}(a))$, which also tends to $\omega(a^*a)$ by [A2] and continuity of inversion. Thus $U_g[a]\to[a]$ for every $[a]\in\mathcal D_\omega$. [F1, A1, A2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Let $\xi\in H_\omega$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Choose $y\in\mathcal D_\omega$ with $\|\xi-y\|<\varepsilon/3$. Since each $U_g$ is unitary, $\|U_g\xi-\xi\|\le2\|\xi-y\|+\|U_gy-y\|$; step 2.2 makes the last term less than $\varepsilon/3$ for $g$ sufficiently near $e$. Hence every orbit is continuous at $e$. For any $g_0\in G$, $\|U_g\xi-U_{g_0}\xi\|=\|U_{g_0^{-1}g}\xi-\xi\|$, so continuity of multiplication transfers continuity to $g_0$. The unitary representation is strongly continuous on all of $G$. [step 1.1, step 2.2, given, algebra] ∎

references.title: Konrad Schmüdgen, An Invitation to Unbounded Representations of *-Algebras on Hilbert Space, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 285, Springer Nature (2020), §4.4
references.locator: §4.4, printed pp. 78–81: GNS common-domain representation and cyclic implementation context.

title: Unital star algebra and positive normalized state — Examples

items.title: Positive Weyl state without a continuous field generator
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice, the hypothesis used to form the Hilbert completion in [[thm-qft-algebraic-gns-domain]]. The claim that positivity and the Weyl relations alone make every GNS one-parameter unitary group $t\mapsto\pi(W(tv))$ strongly continuous for every $v\ne0$ is false, even for the algebraic Weyl algebra of the standard symplectic plane.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Bilinearity of $\sigma$ gives $\sigma(f,g)+\sigma(f+g,h)=\sigma(g,h)+\sigma(f,g+h)$, so the phase factors in $(W(f)W(g))W(h)$ and $W(f)(W(g)W(h))$ agree. Also $(W(f)W(g))^*=e^{i\sigma(f,g)/2}W(-f-g)=W(-g)W(-f)$ by alternation, and $W(0)$ is a two-sided unit. Thus the displayed operations define a unital complex star algebra. [given, A1, algebra]

1.2 For $a=\sum_{f\in F}c_fW(f)$ with finite support $F\subset S$, the Weyl relation gives $a^*a=\sum_{f,g\in F}\overline{c_f}c_g e^{i\sigma(f,g)/2}W(g-f)$. Only the terms $g=f$ contribute to $\omega(a^*a)$, and $\sigma(f,f)=0$, so $\omega(a^*a)=\sum_{f\in F}|c_f|^2\ge0$; also $\omega(W(0))=1$. Hence $\omega$ is a positive normalized state. [given, A1, algebra]

2.1 By [F1], its GNS quotient has dense span of the classes $[W(f)]$. For $f,g\in S$, $([W(f)],[W(g)])_\omega=\omega(W(g)^*W(f))$ is $1$ if $f=g$ and $0$ otherwise; these classes are an orthonormal family with dense span. Left multiplication satisfies $\pi(W(h))[W(f)]=e^{-i\sigma(h,f)/2}[W(h+f)]$, so it permutes this orthonormal family with unit-modulus phases and extends to a unitary on the Hilbert completion, with inverse $\pi(W(-h))$. [F1, given, step 1.2]

3.1 Fix $v\in S\setminus\{0\}$ and put $U(t):=\pi(W(tv))$ for $t\in\mathbb R$. Since $\sigma(tv,sv)=ts\sigma(v,v)=0$, the Weyl relation gives $U(t)U(s)=U(t+s)$ and $U(0)=I$. For every $t\ne0$, $U(t)\Omega=[W(tv)]$ is orthogonal to $\Omega=[W(0)]$, and both are unit vectors; thus $\|U(t)\Omega-\Omega\|=\sqrt2$. This orbit is not continuous at $0$, so $U$ is not strongly continuous. [A1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Suppose a dense linear subspace $E$ had a norm derivative $\lim_{t\to0}(U(t)\xi-\xi)/t$ for every $\xi\in E$. Each such orbit would be continuous at $0$. For any $x\in H_\omega$ and $\varepsilon>0$, choose $\xi\in E$ with $\|x-\xi\|<\varepsilon/3$; unitarity gives $\|U(t)x-x\|\le2\|x-\xi\|+\|U(t)\xi-\xi\|$, so continuity on $E$ would imply continuity at $0$ for every $x$, contradicting step 3.1 at $x=\Omega$. Therefore no dense domain supports a norm-differentiable generator for this unitary group. The example is purely algebraic and asserts no physical preparation or relativistic vacuum. [step 3.1, algebra] ∎

references.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, lecture notes, arXiv:1904.04051v2 (2019), §4.2 Exercise 17
references.locator: §4.2, printed p. 18: the tracial Weyl state defined by delta at the zero vector and its square-summable-function GNS representation.
